subject.title: systemd gateway service can fail to restart after update when env-backed gateway auth token is not loaded

question: Should OpenClaw repair env-backed gateway systemd units during update-mode doctor, and what provenance/storage rule makes that safe for credential-bearing service files?
rationale: The remaining fix can stop real gateway outages, but it decides when OpenClaw may rewrite or suggest rewrites for operator-owned systemd metadata that carries auth-token environment sources.

options.title: Use generated-unit provenance
options.body: Store generated-unit ownership in an approved durable state layer and only auto-update live units whose bytes still match the last OpenClaw-generated record.

options.title: Keep explicit reinstall only
options.body: Continue requiring `openclaw gateway install --force` or manual systemd edits for legacy or drifted units, accepting that update-triggered restarts can preserve a broken env-file shape.

options.title: Add a narrower env-file mode first
options.body: Decide a separate explicit direct EnvironmentFile configuration contract before changing update-mode repair behavior.

recommendation.title: Use generated-unit provenance
recommendation.body: Store generated-unit ownership in an approved durable state layer and only auto-update live units whose bytes still match the last OpenClaw-generated record.

likelyOwner.reason: This person opened the broader provenance follow-up and has adjacent state and service-auth history, making them the clearest owner for the product/security contract decision.
